rationale: Blind and edge-case lenses both ran. Three major patch findings: (1) aria-labelledby is conditionally omitted on pt.root when headerContent is used, so the at(-1) fallback can focus the wrong dialog in stacked scenarios; (2) a[href] is absent from the Priority-2 FOCUSABLE selector, causing link-only dialogs to miss their first focusable; (3) no test covers the at(-1) fallback path. No acceptance/spec lens (no-spec round). Dismissed: tabindex=-1 sentinel concern (sentinels use tabindex=0, not -1), fake-timer style, PrimeReact trigger-focus internal concern (deferred, 1 finding not emitted).

standards_review.notes: Commit subject follows TICKET: description pattern consistent with project history.
No secrets, injection vectors, or unsafe DOM operations. Focus is set via standard HTMLElement.focus().

findings.problem: When headerContent is provided without a header string, pt.root['aria-labelledby'] is undefined (line 208: header ? headerId : undefined). The dialogs.find(el => el.getAttribute('aria-labelledby') === headerId) call returns nothing and the effect falls back to dialogs.at(-1). In any stacked-dialog scenario where the headerContent popup is not the last [role="dialog"] in DOM order, at(-1) picks a different dialog and target?.focus() fires on the wrong element.
findings.impact: Keyboard and screen-reader users land in the wrong dialog when a headerContent popup opens while another popup (rendered after it in the React tree) is already visible. Breaks WCAG 2.1 SC 2.1.2.
findings.recommendation: Set aria-labelledby unconditionally: change `header ? headerId : undefined` to just `headerId` in pt.root. The attribute is consumed only by the focus effect for per-instance identification; the <h4 id={headerId}> element is still gated on header, so accessible-name derivation is unaffected.

findings.problem: The Priority-2 FOCUSABLE selector omits a[href]. Native anchor elements are keyboard-focusable by default without an explicit tabindex, so they are invisible to both the enumerated tag list and the [tabindex] clause.
findings.impact: A dialog whose first interactive element is a plain <a href> link skips it and falls through to the [tabindex="-1"] content-container fallback. Focus lands on a non-interactive wrapper instead of the semantically correct element.

findings.problem: None of the 5 new focus-management tests exercises the dialogs.at(-1) fallback code path. All tests use header="..." (the renderPopup default or explicit prop), so aria-labelledby is always set and find() always succeeds. The headerContent/hideHeader fallback documented in the code comment is untested.
findings.impact: Any regression in the at(-1) path would not be caught by CI, leaving a silent accessibility defect visible only at runtime.
findings.recommendation: Add a test that renders Custom} visible onHide={...}> without a header prop and asserts waitFor(() => expect(document.activeElement).toBe(screen.getByRole('button', { name: 'Close' }))). A second variant with two stacked popups (one headerContent, one header) both visible simultaneously would also validate the ordering assumption.
